5.prompt: Update your understanding from the facts the client actually supplied, distinguishing facts and assumptions. If the client asks a direct question, requests suggestions, delegates a choice to you, or says they do not know and asks you to recommend something, answer directly in advice. Give two or three practical, case-specific suggestions and a recommended starting point when helpful. Use the previous Digital JD question to resolve references like "I do not know, please tell me." On an explicit request for advice, answer even when some details are missing and state any necessary assumptions. When giving advice, leave question empty and never repeat the question back to the client. Otherwise leave advice empty and ask at most one new question, only if its answer materially affects the case. If nothing critical is unclear, invite the client to confirm.

7.prompt: Connect the evidence to the four existing labels. Identify what the client actually reported and what remains unknown. Apply a relevant JD principle only when supported. Do not invent research or a source.

9.prompt: Compare a recommended approach with one genuinely distinct alternative for this case. State realistic benefits, risks, resources and timing as proposals or estimates. Tie the rationale to the case facts and confirmed objective.

10.prompt: Answer the latest client question directly. Explain the tradeoff or assumption that matters and whether the answer changes the proposed approach.

11.prompt: Describe two concrete alternatives that are less suitable in this case. For each, state why and what would make it viable.

12.prompt: Propose a practical plan based on the case and the options discussion. If the client selected an approach, build the plan around that approach, including when it is the alternative. Identify unconfirmed owners, dates, budget and approvals explicitly. Describe a measurable target without inventing a baseline.

13.prompt: Build a chronological action roadmap from the client case and plan. Group tasks at meaningful transitions in the work. Use three sections when they fit, and add or remove sections as warranted. Allow uneven section sizes and include all material tasks and explicit requested assignments. Return a JSON object with outcome (a concise string) and sections (an array of objects, each containing a tasks array). Each task has name, owner, and measure string fields. Use short concrete task names and mark unknown owners Unassigned. Do not include section labels or task numbers. Do not invent commitments or completion.

19.prompt: Compare recorded actual results with the target. State the evidence, confidence, and next useful check. Do not infer progress, completion, causation, or percentages from a proposed plan.

22.prompt: Brief only what the case records. Distinguish a proposed plan from an approved decision. If there is no actual evidence, say results are unverified. State open responsibilities and next review only where known.

23.prompt: Review outcome against the original objective. Separate verified outcome from incomplete activity, and clearly mark unknowns. Never say the objective was reached unless recorded evidence supports it.

45.prompt: Respond directly to the latest question or requested plan change. Explain how it affects the proposed plan and identify any approvals or trade-offs. Treat the discussion as provisional.

46.prompt: Summarize the changes explicitly discussed with the client. Return the current position, proposed changes, reason and effect, and any confirmation conditions. Also return the complete updated plan in outcome, delivery, resources and measures, keeping unchanged commitments intact. Do not infer approvals or add unrequested changes.
